title: Coral bleaching, the 2015 die-off at Dongsha Atoll, and the fourth global bleaching event

sources.title: Corals Die as Global Warming Collides with Local Weather in the South China Sea (news release, 2017-03-23)
World's Fourth Mass Coral Bleaching Event Likely Ended in 2025 (2026-06-02)

facts.text: Tiny algae called zooxanthellae live inside coral tissue; they are the coral's main food source and give corals most of their color.
The algae make food by photosynthesis, and most of that food feeds the coral; the coral gives the algae a place to live.
Coral polyps are nearly transparent, so when the algae are lost the white skeleton shows through and the coral looks white; this is coral bleaching.
A bleached coral is not dead, but it has lost its main food source; if the stress ends soon the coral can recover, and if it lasts the coral dies.
Dongsha Atoll is a shallow, nearly circular coral reef in the South China Sea, about two hours by plane from Taiwan.

In June 2015 the sea surface temperature in the South China Sea rose about 2 degrees C above normal, but on Dongsha Atoll the water reached 36 degrees C, about 6 degrees C above normal summer temperatures.
In 2015 all of the corals on the reef bleached and about 40 percent of them died; dead coral was quickly overgrown by green turf algae.
Scientists saw the bleaching begin at the end of a month-long field visit and found the reef dead, not recovering, when they returned a few weeks later.
Heat budget calculations showed that sunlight and air temperature stayed nearly constant; the loss of cooling by wind and waves was the main cause of the extreme heating.

Normally wind and waves flush the reef with cooler open-ocean water, and Dongsha is usually hit by tropical storms in June; in June 2015 no storms came and there was at times almost no wind and no waves.
The researchers warned that projections based on open-ocean warming of 2 degrees may be too optimistic for shallow reefs, where local weather can amplify the warming to about 6 degrees.
NOAA confirmed the fourth global coral bleaching event on April 15, 2024; earlier global events occurred in 1998, 2010 and 2014–2017.
During the fourth global event, bleaching-level heat stress affected about 84 percent of the world's coral reef area, and mass bleaching was recorded in at least 83 countries and territories.
NOAA says the fourth global bleaching event likely ended in the middle of 2025; the 84 percent figure had been reached by 2025.
